themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: ASML reported Q3 sales of EUR 11.7 billion and net income of EUR 5.0 billion (about EUR 4.13 billion expected), raised 2026 sales to EUR 44 to 45 billion, and said planned supply will not fully meet demand in 2027 and 2028. Memory kept sliding: Micron closed down 3.62% at $953.19 on Oct 13 as Netlist filed patent complaints at the ITC, and SK hynix fell 10.09% that day. Microsoft unveiled its Maia 300 inference chip on Oct 12, built by TSMC for 2027 volume.
themes.for_you: ASML says the lithography chokepoint is still tight, which supports TSM into Thursday's report; ASML itself has no dashboard verdict (Not enough data). Memory is still a no touch for swings. NVDA is left out of both lists: Maia 300 takes some inference spending, but Microsoft still buys NVIDIA for training. Samsung is left out of bearish because it rose 0.65% on Oct 14 while SK hynix fell.

themes.name: Fintech and Crypto Rails: Stablecoins, Tokenization, Exchanges
themes.what: Morgan Stanley beat on Oct 14 (EPS $3.03 vs $2.91) as equities trading rose about 41% to $5.8 billion, while fixed income trading fell about 7%. Bank of America missed (adjusted EPS $1.08 vs $1.10) on weaker trading and took a $1.2 billion regulatory settlement charge; shares fell more than 7% premarket. BlackRock's assets reached a record $15.5 trillion with about $205 billion of net inflows in the quarter.
themes.for_you: Two of three big trading desks now confirm the equities boom, which supports exchanges: CBOE is Buy zone now. BLK is Buy zone, wait for the chart (up/down volume 0.89); record flows could help the chart repair. NDAQ, HOOD and SCHW stay wait for the chart. BAC is not on the map.

themes.name: Healthcare and Medtech: Aging, Heart, Sugar, Hearing, Sight
themes.what: Medtronic's MiniMed split off closed oversubscribed: it accepted 55,032,401 of its own shares at a 4.5939 exchange ratio, with a final proration factor of 18.289133%, and kept no MiniMed stake (Oct 14). That retires about 4.3% of Medtronic's roughly 1.28 billion shares. UnitedHealth gave back an early gain of over 4% and closed down 0.2% at $377.76 on Oct 13.
themes.for_you: MDT is Buy zone now and its share count just shrank; tranches still fit. UNH is left out of both lists: the beat was real but buyers did not hold the gap, and its up/down volume is 0.78, so no put or swing on it yet.

innovations.name: Materials
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. Hexcel confirmed it will report Q3 results on Oct 21 after the close, with the call Oct 22; third party calendars showing Oct 26 or Oct 28 are wrong. MP Materials still guides first commercial magnet shipments to GM for Q4 2026, with no shipment date announced.
innovations.for_you: No action. HXL and MP are left out of both lists because nothing changed in the business; this only fixes the date to watch. Avoid opening a new swing in HXL into Oct 21.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.what: INDEC said September prices rose 1.9% in the month, in line with the 1.9% forecast and up from 1.7% in August. Yearly inflation is 33.4% and prices are up 23.6% in 2026. Housing, water, power and fuel rose most, 3.1%, as subsidies keep falling.
countries.for_you: No action. An in line print removes one risk for GGAL and BMA but gives them no new push, so they are left out of both lists. Higher regulated utility prices help PAM and TGS a little. YPF still trades on oil.

countries.name: European Union
countries.what: ASML, Europe's biggest tech company, reported Q3 sales of EUR 11.7 billion and raised its 2026 sales outlook to EUR 44 to 45 billion, the third raise this year. It said planned supply will not fully meet customer demand in 2027 and 2028. The Amsterdam shares were up about 1.75% to EUR 1,536 before the open.
countries.for_you: No action. ASML has no dashboard verdict (Not enough data, a currency mismatch), so it is not a buy zone call. It is a good sign for TSM before Thursday's report.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: A Houthi ballistic missile hit an Aramco administrative building at its Dhahran headquarters early Oct 14, causing a limited fire and damaging the top floors used by executives; reports differ on injuries (none per AP, four per Riyadh via IBTimes). On Oct 13 UKMTO reported a tanker struck in the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran said hit a mine, and two container ships hit by projectiles. Brent rose 0.58% to $106.30 and WTI 1.57% to $95.62 by 8:03am ET.
countries.for_you: Oil names stay helped, but a headline can cut both ways in one day. XOM is 0.4% from its 172.91 pivot and needs 20.4M+ shares to confirm; do not chase a gap. FRO is left out: rates rise but so does the risk to ships.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: Correction and update: the KOSPI closed Oct 13 at 6,035.35, down 5.46%, not below 6,000 (that was intraday). SK Hynix closed down 10.09% and Samsung 7.39%. On Oct 14 an early rebound of over 2% faded and the index closed down 0.44% at 6,008.81, its sixth straight loss, with Samsung up 0.65% and SK Hynix down 1.66%.
countries.for_you: No action. A failed bounce is a sign the selling is not done, so no MU or memory swings. KB, SHG and WF stay hurt; watch the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision.
